what_its_for: Adefovir dipivoxil is an antiviral medicine used to treat chronic hepatitis B, a long-term liver infection caused by the hepatitis B virus. It works by slowing down the growth of the virus in your body, which helps protect your liver from damage over time.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet. Keep taking it even if you feel well, because stopping early can cause your hepatitis B to come back worse.
dosing: The usual adult dose is one 10 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have kidney problems. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store adefovir dipivoxil at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medicines that can harm your kidneys, such as ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or certain antibiotics, without talking to your doctor first. Do not drink alcohol heavily, as it can make liver damage worse. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without your doctor's guidance, as this can cause a dangerous flare-up of hepatitis B.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, loss of appetite, feeling very tired or weak, muscle pain or weakness, trouble breathing, dark urine, yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dizziness, or a fast or irregular heartbeat. These could be signs of serious side effects such as kidney problems or a build-up of lactic acid in your blood. Also call your doctor if your hepatitis B symptoms seem to get worse.
when_it_works: Adefovir dipivoxil starts working right away to slow the virus, but it may take several weeks to months before you notice improvement in your lab tests or symptoms. Many people feel no different at first but the medicine is still working. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to check how well the medicine is controlling the virus and to monitor your liver and kidneys.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor will need to lower your dose or change how often you take this medicine if your kidneys are not working well. Regular kidney function tests are important while you are on this medicine. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy is not fully known. There is a pregnancy registry for women who take this medicine while pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine is not approved for children under 12 years of age. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to kidney-related side effects and should be monitored closely.
